newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals firmer again, except for gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals firmer again, except for gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended firmer for the second session in a row Monday, except for gold, which remains the weakest contract in the complex, traders said.
"Activity was light but support for silver and further gains for platinum and palladium may eventually help gold to bounce also," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
COMEX April gold ended down 90 cents at $343.10 an ounce, but held above the contract low at $339.40 seen Friday.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $340.85/35, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $340.40, and the New York close Friday at $341.50/00. On Friday gold fixed at $339.75, the lowest fix since April 22, 1993.

"Prospects for mounting supply pressure from central banks and producers, combined with investor liquidation due to low inflationary expectations and bullish sentiment toward paper assets, have sustained the gold price downtrend," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
However, the end of the Muslim holiday of Ramadan and the end of the Chinese New Year holiday in Asia this week may see the return of some physical demand, analysts said.
From its five year highs around $416 an ounce in February 1996, gold prices have fallen 18 percent to three year lows last week around $340 an ounce.
The gold price fall has unnerved producers who who do not have a history of hedging their output, analysts noted.
While North American and Australian producers are known to actively hedge their forward output, South African miners are traditionally reluctant to do so, analysts said.
Last year the South African gold mining industry received some protection from a declining currency, but the price of gold in South African rand fell to new 11 month lows around 1500 rand Monday.

North American producers have been able to boost their earnings by about 10 percent by use of hedging techniques such a spot deferred contracts to sell their output forward, analyst John Dobra said in a report issued by the US Gold Institute Monday.

The average cash and non-cash breakeven cost for US gold producers at the end of 1995 was around $308 an ounce, Dobra said. This compares with an average cost for gold miners worldwide of $315 an ounce, consultants Gold Fields Mineral Services said last week.
The weakness in gold saw the spot gold/silver ratio fall to new 16 month lows around 68.80 Monday.
COMEX March silver ended up 1.8 cents at $4.960, after significant investment fund buying of silver futures in recent weeks, analysts said.
Gold remained weaker than platinum also Monday, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread soaring $4.20 an ounce to a new four month high at $16.20 an ounce.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum ended up $3.60 at $359.30, while NYMEX March palladium gained a further $3.45 an ounce to a $138.50, after seeing a contract high at $139.00.
The Norilsk Nickel Combine in Russia continues to face serious financial problems and is now facing renewed labor unrest due to pay arrears, the US Platinum Institute said in a weekly report.
Meqnwhile delays in a contract deal between the Japanese palladium users and their Russian suppliers have led to sharp gains in palladium's price, the Platinum Institute noted.
